1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c5 5.b3.strategy: Protects the c4-pawn and prepares the queen's bishop for the long diagonal. White does not rush to take the centre; the cost is a slower game, in which Black's c-pawn has already taken d4 under control.
Develops the knight and adds to the pressure on d4, so Black fights for the centre with pawns and pieces alike. A natural, flexible choice that keeps the c-pawn well supported.
